title: T Holder, drummer A.G. Godley and Jimmy Westbrook's T&T band
summary: Albert confirms Holder's singer and sidemen, praises a left-handed drummer who played with Trent, and describes the T&T band with Herschel.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I had a whole bunch of names of people that I wanted to ask you about, that played around Texas and Kansas City and Connecticut. Did you ever think of the name of T Holder's singer? Do you know who that would have been? Featero?
He was with T Holder. Oh sure, that band there is where Andy Craig slipped away from T Holder. Oh yeah. And that's the same musicians.
Yeah, so he had played T Holder. What about A.G. Gonday's reputation? What kind of drummer was he?
Great drummer, left-handed drummer. It was great in those days.
And who did he play with? Tren? Mostly with Tren. Tren. That was the only band I've known God I'd ever play with.
And you had a Jimmy Westbrook out of, what's the name of that, Waco, Texas. And that's the one where Herschel was with them. He was called the T&T Band.
Yeah, I was going to ask you about that band. You were talking about the Tren. Right.
Well Herschel was playing alto in that band. And Jimmy Westbrook was playing the drums. He was not the left-handed drumming.
Who else was in the T&T? I can't recall. Big band, a small band?
Well in those days, yes. Ten pieces were considered big.
